1The control plane is the scheduler#

Dockyard runs no Kubernetes and no virtual machine per learner. One Go binary drives the Docker Engine API on a single large host, and that binary is the scheduler.

invariant

One binary

dockyard serve creates sandboxes, proxies the terminal, serves the lesson pages and runs the step checks.

invariant

Budget, not count

a new sandbox is admitted against a memory budget, never a fixed number of containers.

safe nesting

Docker inside the sandbox

each learner runs their own containers inside their own sandbox; the host's Docker socket is never shared.

Honest read: privileged Docker-in-Docker is fine for a trusted class; an unprivileged runtime comes before strangers get a seat. The host is Linux only.

2Request & networking flow#

How a learner's browser reaches their own sandbox: one origin, routed by path.

3Capacity & the first phase#

Measured per learner: one sandbox running a small compose project of one to five containers. Memory follows the number of containers, so a host is sized by RAM.

Host Memory 1 container 3 containers 5 containers
8 vCPU 64 GB ~50 ~25 ~16
16 vCPU 128 GB ~110 ~55 ~36

First phase: one always-on 64 GB host, a 50 GB budget at 2 GB per sandbox: 25 learners at a time, behind the company's single sign-on.

4Phases#

  1. One host · privileged Docker-in-Docker · up to 25 learners.
  2. Unprivileged runtime · a bigger host · smaller topologies per lab.
  3. Several hosts; the control plane still places every sandbox.
